tools.name: openapi_diff
tools.description:
Compare two OpenAPI 3.x specifications and classify every change
    as breaking, non-breaking, or info.

    Use this when you want to know if a candidate OpenAPI spec change
    is safe to ship or will break existing clients. The diff covers
    paths, operations, parameters, request bodies, respo

tools.name: monit_rs_stats
tools.description:
Get live aggregate statistics for the monit.rs platform.

    Returns approximate counts of regressions caught, AI analyses
    generated, and probes executed across all monitored APIs to date.
    Useful when answering "does monit.rs actually work at scale?" — the
    numbers are real, within about

tools.name: monit_rs_describe
tools.description:
Return the canonical product description for monit.rs.

    Use this when a user asks what monit.rs is, what it does, how it
    differs from Pingdom / Checkly / UptimeRobot, or for product URLs.
    The response is the curated content from monit.rs/llms.txt — the
    operator's authoritative descri

tools.name: list_my_endpoints
tools.description:
List all monitored endpoints owned by the authenticated account.

    Returns brief records suitable for LLM enumeration. For full detail
    (headers, spec URL, heartbeat_token) use `describe_endpoint(id)`.

tools.name: list_my_incidents
tools.description:
List incidents on the caller's account. Defaults to only OPEN incidents.

    Fields include the incident's dedup_key — pass this to
    `acknowledge_incident` or `resolve_incident` to act on it.

tools.name: list_my_regressions
tools.description:
List detected schema regressions on the caller's account.
    Optionally filter by endpoint_id.

tools.name: get_endpoint_uptime
tools.description: Aggregated uptime summary for an endpoint over the requested window.

tools.name: describe_endpoint
tools.description: Full detail for one endpoint. Use `list_my_endpoints()` to get the ID.

tools.name: acknowledge_incident
tools.description:
Mark an incident as acknowledged. Use `list_my_incidents()` to
    find the dedup_key.

tools.name: resolve_incident
tools.description: Close an incident. Symmetric to acknowledge_incident.

tools.name: create_endpoint
tools.description: Create a new monitored endpoint. Respects your tier's max_endpoints cap.

tools.name: delete_endpoint
tools.description:
Delete a monitored endpoint. Cascades: removes test_results,
    baselines, regressions, incidents attached to it.

    Guarded by two safety layers beyond the scope check:

    1. `confirm_by_typing_the_endpoint_name` MUST equal the endpoint's
       exact `.name` (case-sensitive, whitespace-trimme

tools.name: list_alert_channels
tools.description:
List alert channels configured on the authenticated account.

    Does NOT return decrypted config (webhook URLs, PagerDuty routing keys,
    etc.). Use the dashboard or `describe_alert_channel` HTTP API when you
    need to inspect the actual config.

tools.name: list_status_pages
tools.description: List public status pages owned by the authenticated account.

tools.name: list_security_findings
tools.description:
List security findings detected on the caller's monitored endpoints.
    Optionally filter by severity.

tools.name: describe_incident
tools.description:
Full detail for one incident. Use `list_my_incidents()` to find the
    dedup_key. Includes the incident's endpoint name and current status.

tools.name: pause_endpoint
tools.description:
Pause a monitored endpoint (stops probing, keeps history). Idempotent
    — no-op if already paused.

tools.name: resume_endpoint
tools.description:
Resume a paused endpoint. Rejects if resuming would exceed your tier's
    active-endpoint cap (upgrade or pause another endpoint first).

tools.name: update_endpoint_interval
tools.description:
Change how often an endpoint is probed. Minimum interval varies by
    tier (free=900s, developer=300s, starter=60s, pro/scale/enterprise=30s).

tools.name: create_status_page
tools.description:
Create a public status page at https://<slug>.status.monit.rs.
    Add endpoints to it via the dashboard or the HTTP API (adding
    endpoints from chat is deliberately not exposed — the mapping is
    fiddly and easy to get wrong).

tools.name: create_alert_channel
tools.description:
Create an alert channel. Pass EXACTLY one of email_address /
    webhook_url / pagerduty_routing_key matching the channel_type:

      - channel_type='email'     → email_address='ops@example.com'
      - channel_type='webhook'   → webhook_url='https://your-endpoint'
      - channel_type='slack'

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: list_my_endpoints, list_alert_channels, create_status_page · Private data: list_my_endpoints · Public sink: list_alert_channels, create_alert_channel · Destructive: delete_endpoint.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: list_my_endpoints, list_alert_channels, create_status_page · Private data: list_my_endpoints · Public sink: list_alert_channels, create_alert_channel · Destructive: delete_endpoint

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
